chapter_title: The Living Organisms — Characteristics and Habitats

concepts.title: Adaptation
concepts.definition: The development of specific physical traits or behavioral habits that allow an organism to thrive in its natural environment.
concepts.key_idea: Organisms evolve specific features to survive in their unique habitats.
question_patterns: what is adaptation
define adaptation in organisms
how do specific features help an animal survive
why is adaptation necessary for survival
list the main features of adaptation

solution_steps.explain: determine the environmental conditions of the region.
link physical features (e.g., gills, thick fur) to environmental challenges (e.g., water, cold).
confirm that each matched trait directly improves the organism's ability to obtain food, water, or shelter in that habitat.

concepts.title: Habitat Classification
concepts.definition: The natural environment where an organism lives, categorized primarily by whether it is on land or in water.
concepts.key_idea: Habitats provide essential resources like food, water, and shelter.
question_patterns: distinguish between terrestrial and aquatic habitats
what is a habitat
give examples of aquatic habitats
classify the given environment as terrestrial or aquatic
explain habitat classification in your own words

solution_steps.explain: determine if the organism lives on land or in water.
assign to terrestrial if land-based, aquatic if water-based.
provide representative organisms for the category (e.g., desert fox and camel for terrestrial, fish and lotus for aquatic) to confirm the classification.

concepts.title: Biotic and Abiotic Components
concepts.definition: The ecosystem is made up of living organisms (biotic) and non-living factors (abiotic) that influence them.
concepts.key_idea: Living things interact with non-living factors like sunlight, air, and water.
question_patterns: list the abiotic components of a habitat
differentiate between biotic and abiotic factors
are rocks biotic or abiotic
how do abiotic factors affect plant growth
list the main features of biotic and abiotic components

solution_steps.explain: separate items into living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic).
describe how biotic components depend on abiotic factors, such as plants needing sunlight, water, and air.
confirm that both biotic and abiotic components are present and interacting, since an ecosystem requires both to function.

concepts.title: Characteristics of Living Things
concepts.definition: A set of observable processes including respiration, excretion, growth, and reproduction that distinguish life from non-life.
concepts.key_idea: Living things share common life processes that non-living things lack.
question_patterns: list common characteristics of living things
why is respiration important
how do plants show response to stimuli
is a car living because it moves
justify why characteristics of living things matters

solution_steps.explain: check if the object performs all life processes.
verify growth, respiration, excretion, response to stimuli, and reproduction individually against the object.
if any essential life process is absent, classify the object as non-living even if it shows one life-like trait such as movement.
